messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated gateway 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate. paging @mike (oncall) :rotating_light:
mike: saw the page, jumping in. any customer impact notes yet?
sarah: getting customer-facing error spikes on 3 regions (us-east1, eu-west1, ap-sg). dashboard shows 5xx rate from gateway up from 0.4% -> 7.1% in last 6m.
mike: starting triage. can someone grab a few correlation IDs from recent spikes?
raj: pulling logs now, sending first bundle to /logs/dropbox/3754321000 (private). here's a few sample corrids: corrid=3a1f9e, corrid=4b2eaa, corrid=7f8c01
elaine: thanks raj. quick question — are retries visible from client side or amplified at the gateway?
raj: initial look: many entries show upstream 504 timeout followed by gateway 502/503. looks like upstream service is timing out and gateway surfaces 5xx. also see repeated client retries within 1-2s window.
sarah: customer impact estimate: ~2.3k requests/min failing at peak. ~12 unique customer orgs affected (high-usage customers). tagging support for heads-up.
mike: mitigation in progress: increased gateway retry window to 5s and enabled fallback-to-qpool on route /v1/generate to reduce fanout. scaling dedicated pool now (+3 replicas).
incident-bot: ACTION: runtime scale-up triggered by mike — request id 8f7d2 (ETA ~45s)
raj: dropping a short log snippet for corrid=3a1f9e:
```
[2026-03-17T15:06:21Z] gateway req=3a1f9e route=/v1/generate status=502 upstream=upstream-a timeout=15s attempts=3
[2026-03-17T15:06:22Z] client retry delay=120ms client_id=prod-service-1
[2026-03-17T15:06:23Z] gateway req=3a1f9e fallback_attempt=1 routed_to=qp-reflect-1 status=200 latency=340ms
```
mike: interesting — upstream timeouts are ~15s, but clients retry aggressively which amplifies load. hypothesis A: upstream slow tail + retry amplification at gateway causing queue buildup -> 5xx.
elaine: agree. Hypothesis B: a recent config change on upstream-a reduced its threadpool. I'll check deploy logs.
raj: pulling upstream-a deploys: no deploys in last 24h. but there was a scaling policy change 3h ago (max replicas lowered).
sarah: can we compute a timeline: when did 5xx start vs scaling policy change? if change predates spike, correlation stronger.
mike: timeline from metrics: scaling-policy-change @ 11:30, 5xx spike starts ~14:54. gap of ~3h. could be related (slow drift) or independent (external traffic spike).
elaine: I'm fetching trace samples for corrid list — will paste traces (span IDs, node latencies) in a bit.
raj: uploaded full kvlog tar to dropbox path (same as above). also exported request traces for corrids. link: https://internal.redwood/logs/3754321000 (restricted)
sarah: customer impact note posted to status page draft. recommend we flip to fallback route for all affected customers until upstream issue resolved. :thumbsup:
mike: rolling config change to force fallback for high-error orgs now. if stable in 3m we can keep until upstream autoscaling addressed.
incident-bot: UPDATE — page acknowledged, mitigation actions set: scale-up, route fallback, client retry window advisory.
elaine: trace for corrid=4b2eaa shows long wait on upstream-a worker queue: span worker_wait=12.4s, exec_time=0.3s. that fits queued requests backlog.
raj: additional evidence: connection saturation metrics show TCP conn count near 95% on upstream-a at spike.
sarah: recording hypotheses in-thread: [A] retry amplification + upstream slow tail -> queue buildup; [B] upstream scaling policy lowered capacity; [C] transient network egress causing timeouts. next steps: collect full trace set, confirm scaling policy change intent, and hold mitigation until stable.
mike: good plan. I'll keep the oncall rotation in the loop and hand off at 16:00 if still active. tagging @elaine for deep dive postmortem.
elaine: will prepare RCA deck with timeline, corrid samples, KV logs, and recommendation to change autoscale thresholds + add prefix caching for heavy customers.
sarah: thanks all — if anything changes ping here. otherwise we'll convert to RCA thread after mitigation. :white_check_mark:
